article.Citation/Title: Marvania, N. P., Rayan, A. L., Merchant, D. V., Shah, D. P., Mehta, P. I., & Modh, F. D. (2024). Ketamine therapy in patients of alcohol use disorder: A prospective pilot study to evaluate abstinence rate with this add-on treatment modality. Annals of Indian Psychiatry, 8(4), 324-327.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Marva. Ketamine Therapy in Patients of Alcohol Use Disorder_ A Prospective Pilot Study to Evaluate Abstinence Rate with This Add-on Treatment Modality.pdf
article.Outcome: 51.98% increase in mean AASE (Alcohol Abstinence Self-Efficacy Scale) confidence score from baseline to the final 2-week follow-up assessment
article.InterventionDescription: IV ketamine 0.5 mg/kg in 50 cc normal saline over 50 minutes, 3 doses 3 days apart, post-detoxification add-on in psychiatric outpatient de-addiction setting.

article.Outcome: Abstract and Table 1: the abstract's headline result is 'a final assessment showing a 51.98% increase in confidence from baseline,' matching Table 1's row 'Pre versus finalpost 2 week' (change 51.98%). AASE confidence-to-abstain is the study's stated primary aim ('to evaluate the efficacy of ketamine in enhancing confidence levels to abstain from alcohol'), and the 2-week final assessment is the outcome the abstract and conclusion close on, so it was chosen over the intermediate post-session-1/2/3 comparisons in the same table, which reflect cumulative in-treatment change rather than the sustained/primary endpoint.
article.SD: Table 1, 'Pre versus finalpost 2 week' row, 'T statistics' column = -4.982. No degrees of freedom were printed for this paired t-test in Table 1 (N=18 would imply df=17, but this is not stated in the article, so it is not appended).
article.PVal: Table 1, same row, 'P' column = '<0.05'; the article states this threshold applies 'across all comparisons.'
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Results: 'The study included 18 participants.' No dropout or loss to follow-up is reported anywhere in the text; abstinence status ('seven participants had maintained abstinence... the rest gave a history of consuming alcohol') is reported for what appears to be the full enrolled sample, so N=18 is used as the analyzed sample for the final-assessment comparison.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Setting (GMERS Medical College psychiatric OPD, Ahmedabad), eligibility, intervention protocol, outcome measures (AASE/AUDIT), statistics (paired t-test/ANOVA), results, harms ('no report of any adverse effects'), and funding/COI ('Nil'; 'no conflicts of interest') are all explicitly described. Comparator absence is counted as described because the Discussion explicitly flags the lack of an 'adequate control' arm as a needed addition for future work. No sample-size/power justification is given, and randomization and blinding are never mentioned or characterized as absent anywhere in the text (the single-arm, unblinded design must be inferred from the Methods rather than stated), so those three criteria are coded N. n_met=11 < 13, so the binary is 0.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 1 on the primary AASE confidence outcome, which showed a statistically significant increase sustained to 2-week follow-up (p<0.05). Flagging a tension: the Discussion itself questions the clinical meaningfulness of this positive result, since only 7/18 (38.8%) maintained abstinence at follow-up, a lower rate than comparator ketamine studies cited (53.9-70%) and than psychotherapy-alone benchmarks (~28%) cited in the same paragraph. Pos Result Y/N reflects the primary designated outcome (AASE), not the abstinence rate.
article.RandomizationYN: No random allocation is described anywhere; all 18 enrolled patients received the same ketamine protocol. Per PromptVersion v1.2, a single-arm design codes this element's absence as 0, not 3.
article.BlindingYN: No blinding of any kind (patient, rater, assessor) is mentioned; open-label single-arm design. Coded 0, not 3, per the v1.2 single-arm boundary rule.
article.Double+Blind: 0 because BlindingYN=0; open-label study, no blinding of any kind was implemented.
article.Comparator: No control or comparison arm; ketamine was given to all 18 participants as an add-on to standard detoxification. Coded 0 (design element absent), not 3, per the v1.2 single-arm boundary rule. The Discussion explicitly frames this absence as a limitation, calling for 'a longer study with adequate control... in a controlled setting' in future work.
article.PrimaryCare: Study was conducted entirely within a psychiatric outpatient de-addiction department (specialist mental-health care), with no interface to primary-care providers or settings described.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power calculation, and no discussion of the study being underpowered, appears anywhere in the text (this is an 18-patient pilot with no such discussion).
article.Retention (%): Study was not randomized, so the denominator is the enrolled N (18). No dropout, loss to follow-up, or incomplete final assessment is reported; abstinence/relapse status at the final assessment is given for what reads as the full sample of 18, so retention = 18/18 = 100%.
article.BaseStatus: Results: 'AUDIT score for all the participants was above 20.' AUDIT >=20 conventionally corresponds to likely alcohol dependence (the most severe AUDIT band), so baseline severity is coded 'Severe.'
article.Age_Median: Results: 'mean age of 34.5 years' falls in the 30-50 bracket.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Article reports no race or ethnicity data for the sample at all (only sex and age are given), so coded '.' rather than inferring a value from the study's India location.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted at GMERS Medical College and Hospital, Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India; coded 'NonUS' with the country name recorded here rather than in the field itself.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Participants were drawn from routine psychiatric OPD de-addiction visits (consecutive treatment-seekers aged 18+), with exclusions only for other substance use, non-depression/anxiety comorbid psychiatric disorders, and physical unfitness for the procedure -- a fairly representative clinical de-addiction population rather than a narrowly screened volunteer/advertisement sample.
article.InterventionTherapy: The protocol consists of standard benzodiazepine detoxification followed by ketamine infusions plus informed-consent counseling about the procedure; no structured psychotherapy, integration, or motivational-enhancement component is described, unlike the comparator studies discussed (e.g., Dakwar et al. and Grabski et al. paired ketamine with MET/psychological therapy). Coded 0.
article.HarmsAssessed: Discussion: 'There was no report of any adverse effects to ketamine in the dose of 0.5 mg/kg,' which is an explicit (if brief) safety assessment, consistent with SafetyReported='Y'.
article.ReductionMeasured: The study reports only a binary abstinence/relapse status ('maintained abstinence' vs. 'gave a history of consuming alcohol') rather than a distinct partial-reduction/harm-reduction endpoint (e.g., drinks per week, heavy-drinking days), so coded 0.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1 because return-to-use status was explicitly tracked at the final follow-up ('the rest gave a history of consuming alcohol'), even though no drinking-days or quantity detail is given beyond this binary status.
article.AE_denominator: Not explicitly stated as a separate 'safety population'; taken as the full enrolled/treated sample of 18, since the article's single blanket statement of no adverse effects appears to cover all ketamine-treated participants.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Inferred as 0 from AnyAEReported='N' (article states no adverse effects were reported for the ketamine dose used); not itself given as an explicit count in the text.
article.EligibleYN: Passes (a): prospectively planned add-on intervention (ketamine, fixed dose/schedule) delivered under an IRB-approved protocol (IECHRPGR reference number given) with defined enrollment (Nov 2023-Jan 2024), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, and prospective outcome assessment (AASE at baseline, after each session, and at 2-week follow-up) -- this is a clinical trial despite lacking randomization/blinding/comparator (single-arm trials are eligible per the v1.2 boundary case). Passes (b): AASE (a validated alcohol self-efficacy/craving instrument), AUDIT scores, and abstinence/relapse status are all substance-use outcomes.

config_proposal.note: This is a single-arm pre/post design: the reported paired t-test (T=-4.982, p<0.05, 51.98% AASE increase) is a within-subject change over time, not a between-groups effect size, so none of the seven supported Tier-1 conversion methods apply defensibly.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Statistically significant within-subject increase in AASE confidence-to-abstain score sustained from baseline to 2-week post-treatment follow-up (51.98% increase, T=-4.982, p<0.05), in a single-arm study with no comparator group.
